title: Development and Validation of Two Single-Item Scales Measuring Content-Unrelated Social Media Second-Screen Use During Solitary Viewing and Co-Viewing
content: OBJECTIVE To develop two single-item scales measuring content-unrelated social media second-screen use during solitary viewing (Social Media Second-Screen Use Scale – Solitary Viewing; SMSSU-SV) and during co-viewing (Social Media Second-Screen Use Scale – Co-Viewing; SMSSU-CV), and to examine their validity. METHOD We conducted a web-based cross-sectional study with a convenience sample of 922 adults in Greece. Both items were rated from 0 (never) to 10 (always). We examined the distribution of scores, floor and ceiling effects, construct validity through 26 hypotheses on correlations and differences between known groups, and two hypotheses on the relationship between the two scales. RESULTS The mean score was 4.65 on the SMSSU-SV and 3.01 on the SMSSU-CV. The SMSSU-SV showed no floor or ceiling effects, whereas 20.4% of participants scored 0 on the SMSSU-CV. Both scales showed moderate positive correlations with social media addiction, social media distraction, fear of missing out, no-social-media phobia, social media fatigue, and daily time spent on social media, and weak correlations with anxiety and depression, loneliness, and sleep quality. Scores were higher among participants with possible problematic social media use and among participants aged 18 to 29 years. The two scales were strongly correlated (rho=0.674), and scores during solitary viewing were higher than during co-viewing. All hypotheses were confirmed. CONCLUSIONS The SMSSU-SV and the SMSSU-CV are brief and valid tools to measure content-unrelated social media second-screen use during solitary viewing and co-viewing. Further studies should further examine their reliability and validity.
